findings.title: Hyperedge mass is lost by graph sparsification
findings.assumptions: n=201; complete unit pair hyperedges plus {1,2,3} of weight 1/100; rank 3; alpha1=0.1; admissible graph sparsifier drops only two weak labelled star edges
findings.decisive_evidence: Maximum relative spectral loss 1/13401; underlying input count 20102 satisfies alpha>=sqrt(n/m); output count 20100=n/alpha^2; missing group's update denominator is zero and score is zero instead of positive 1/10050.
findings.alternative_readings: Admissible subroutine output, not measured probability for a particular implementation. Maintaining pre-sparsification weights would require another algorithm and complexity analysis.
findings.impact_bound: Displayed leverage construction and domination proof invalid; impossibility of quantum sparsification not claimed

findings.title: Constant sampling normalizer bias
findings.assumptions: Exact valid score oracle; sample count <=m; rank-three family {0,i,j}; all unit weights; z=4/(n-2); normalizer ratio 21/20 permitted by 0.1 interface; epsilon=1/100; sufficiently large n
findings.decisive_evidence: Every sampled sequence has output energy 21m/20 at x_0=1, other coordinates 0; relative error 1/20. Uncentered expectation cannot be replaced by a Rademacher-signed expectation.
findings.alternative_readings: A particular normalizer could be accidentally exact; the stated interface and proof do not require it.
findings.impact_bound: Arbitrary epsilon conclusion is not established by the algorithm's fixed normalizer tolerance

repair.statement: eta+(1+eta)beta<=epsilon for eta=beta=epsilon/3, 0<epsilon<=1; other core problems remain

findings.title: Runtime density simplification
findings.decisive_evidence: Ratio equals epsilon sqrt(r). All triple hyperedges plus V gives r=n, m=Theta(n^3), epsilon=1/2; stated density assumptions hold, ratio is nonpolylogarithmic.
findings.core_dependency: Abstract p1 advertises the rank-dependent main algorithm runtime -> Remark4.2 removes a nonpolylogarithmic term from Theorem4.1.

repair.statement: Retain both terms or require epsilon<=1/sqrt(r), up to suppressed logarithms.

findings.impact_bound: Demonstrated invalid simplification of a core advertised runtime; full two-term bound is not refuted. A short summary correction does not validate the stronger rank-dependent claim.

findings.title: Disconnected graph domain in Proposition C.2
findings.decisive_evidence: Unit edge {1,2}, isolated vertex 3; x=(1,1,-2) perpendicular to 1 but in kernel, giving 0>=6 false.

repair.statement: Restrict x to range(L_G), and restrict chaining domain correspondingly when kernel matches the hypergraph.

findings.core_dependency: Proposition C.2 p17 -> explicit T subset B2 assertion p19 -> Lemma C.1 chaining application -> Theorem4.1.
findings.impact_bound: As-written core chaining derivation uses a false domain claim; range restriction is locally valid under the matching-kernel condition, but full chaining and the entire algorithm are not certified.

findings.title: High-probability upgrade and downstream accuracy costs
findings.decisive_evidence: Proof ends at expectation bound; direct substitution into stated classical runtimes keeps epsilon^-2 / epsilon^-3.
findings.impact_bound: No additional supported severity assigned; requires an appropriate probability argument and downstream algorithms.
